mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances following a FEDFUNDS increase > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within two months signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances following a UNRATE increase > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downward.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances following two consecutive quarters of declining GDPC1.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased production capacity supports economic growth.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances following an INDPRO increase > 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls by more than 100,000 in a month signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances following a PAYEMS decrease > 100,000.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts by more than 10% in a month signals a strengthening demand environment, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased construction activity supports economic growth.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances following a HOUST increase > 10%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds the inflation rate (CPIAUCSL), it signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real interest rates rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > CPIAUCSL.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP growth (GDPC1) is positive but the unemployment rate (UNRATE) increases by more than 0.3% in a month, it signals a demand-driven growth with labor market weakness, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the mixed signals.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 positive and UNRATE increase > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when GDPC1 is positive and UNRATE increases > 0.3%.
